scope: Product and runtime parity audit. Source support is not matched runtime proof. No row certifies overall equality.

rows.t3: Main and V2 use the Agent SDK; V2 supports exact native forks as well as steering and compaction.
rows.mako: Direct SDK steering, compaction and native resume passed real provider checks. Exact native fork-at-turn is not advertised.
rows.required: Implement and verify exact native forks without changing the source session; rerun packaged lifecycle and approval checks.

rows.t3: Main and V2 use app-server; V2 exposes optional compaction.
rows.mako: Steering and same-native-session resume/recall passed. Manual compaction is withheld after a real context-loss test.
rows.required: Resolve compaction history loss and prove post-compaction recall before enabling it.

rows.t3: V2 uses Cursor SDK create/resume and /compress, but explicitly rejects steering and interactive approval callbacks.
rows.mako: ACP driver advertises no native resume, no steering and no manual compaction. Portable continuation is a different guarantee.
rows.required: Prove SDK/native resume and compaction while retaining explicit policy behavior; never silently remove approval handling.

evidence.anchor: Cursor Agent SDK does not expose interactive approval requests.

rows.t3: Main uses OpenCode SDK and ACP for Grok; Antigravity is present. Devin is not among the inspected adapters.
rows.mako: OpenCode/Grok/Devin use provider-owned transports. Earlier six-provider browser runs passed, but native controls differ. Antigravity is not registered.
rows.required: Compare native controls and fresh lifecycle behavior per provider; do not infer parity from a shared interface.

rows.t3: V2 has command receipts and active-turn checks. Runtime failure equivalence has not been exercised against T3.
rows.mako: Steering intents persist before dispatch; uncertain delivery is never replayed; exact request/run checks and duplicate IDs are tested.
rows.required: Run the same dropped-acknowledgement, stale-turn and restart cases against both implementations.

rows.t3: V2 has context handoff and provider-switch services.
rows.mako: Durable full/delta handoff, attachments and source-history retention exist and have focused tests.
rows.required: Matched long-history switch-and-return tasks must retain instructions, media and tool meaning.

rows.t3: V2 has runtime recovery and restart-continuation policies.
rows.mako: Mako journals requests and controls; interrupted/uncertain delivery is retained instead of replayed.
rows.required: Kill each host at dispatch, permission and completion boundaries and compare outcomes and user recovery steps.

rows.t3: T3 has dedicated approval and structured-input composer panels; support is provider-specific.
rows.mako: Shared permission UI and provider-owned responses exist; new Claude SDK maps interactive questions and session grants.
rows.required: Keyboard, denial, session grants, child-originated requests and pending-request restart need a matched matrix.

rows.t3: T3 has provider instances, auth setup and model-option controls.
rows.mako: Typed provider settings, model discovery and scoped saved accounts exist; onboarding and native OAuth coverage are not equivalent.
rows.required: Compare login, expiry, account switching, unsupported settings and model changes during an active turn.

rows.t3: AgentsPanel displays native subagent lifecycle, stable rows, activity, models, tokens and workflow groups.
rows.mako: The new Tasks dialog lists Mako-delegated conversations; transcript tool rendering is not an equivalent native agent monitor.
rows.required: Project provider-native subagent identity/lifecycle and build a registered companion with live and completed states.

rows.t3: V2 has native subagent projection and execution-node relationships. These are distinct from user-created independent jobs.
rows.mako: Mako can delegate into isolated workspaces, cancel children and return findings; the redesigned entry dialog is not visually verified.
rows.required: Exercise two providers concurrently, cancellation, restart, result delivery and failed returns without draft loss.

rows.t3: T3 has proposed-plan cards with export/save and compact task progress.
rows.mako: Mako retains plan entries and renders plan tools, but this does not provide the same proposed-plan workflow.
rows.required: Compare plan approval/revision, saved plan artifacts and live task progress; retain provider ownership.

rows.t3: T3 uses Git checkpoints; inspected main restores then rolls back the provider. V2 validates matching identities.
rows.mako: Real Claude/Codex rewind passed. Mako preserves staging, retains the source conversation and has crash-compensated restore tests.
rows.required: Run identical external-edit, crash and staging cases against T3 before describing this as a comparative win.

rows.t3: Main deletes stale checkpoint refs after revert. A total bounded retention guarantee has not been established for T3.
rows.mako: Mako caps individual captures but has no total snapshot retention/GC policy and no matched repository-latency evidence.
rows.required: Set and test retention that preserves live/recoverable references; measure cold/warm capture, disk growth and restore latency.

rows.t3: T3 has message timelines, bounded earlier-history loading and rich media display.
rows.mako: Mako reconciles message identity and renders shared exchanges. Earlier media/steering tests pass; provider-native histories still require matched coverage.
rows.required: Compare long streamed answers, reasoning, screenshots, attachments, tools, copy, reload and fork history on all providers.

rows.t3: T3 puts controls in composer, agents in a companion; latest main explicitly stabilizes footer layout during loading.
rows.mako: Duplicate header and permanent success rows removed; delegation is on demand. Latest layout has not been visually verified after the memory incident.
rows.required: Verify real idle/working/permission/failed states at narrow and wide widths, keyboard focus, draft preservation and layout stability.

rows.t3: T3 owns preview automation and an injected Playwright runtime. Source presence is not a matched reliability result.
rows.mako: Earlier six-provider extension workflows passed trusted input, image interpretation and exact-target ownership; observations are bounded to 60 KB.
rows.required: Repeat the same navigation/input/image/timeout cases under equal model settings and count retries and wrong-target actions.

rows.t3: Injected runtime and preview automation need a method-by-method comparison; previous frame findings concerned Orca, not proof of T3 behavior.
rows.mako: Mako has explicit iframe targets, refs, raw CDP, events and an exec worker. Automatic combined-frame observation and high-level helper parity remain unproven.
rows.required: Inventory and run nested/cross-origin frames, locator ambiguity, shadow DOM, dialogs, downloads and network waits against both.

rows.t3: T3 has integrated preview, device toolbar, browser recording, import and annotation paths.
rows.mako: Mako has control previews and browser-extension setup; equivalent device/recording/import workflows were not found in the reviewed components.
rows.required: Compare the actual user workflows and decide which fit Mako; test packaged extension installation and reconnect.

rows.t3: Packaged native-computer scripting/permission ergonomics have not been matched in this audit.
rows.mako: Earlier disposable-app click/type/readback passed. Native CUA forwarding is not universal platform or background-input certification.
rows.required: Run exact-window, background input, dialogs, clipboard, permission denial and reconnect workflows in packaged builds.

rows.t3: T3 has Git workflow and review services with integrated controls.
rows.mako: Mako stages, commits, pushes, annotates diffs and manages GitHub PRs. No matched workflow timing/error coverage.
rows.required: Compare large diffs, conflicts, unborn HEAD, partial staging, branch changes, review comments and failed push recovery.

rows.t3: T3 has GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps provider implementations.
rows.mako: Reviewed Mako PR integration is GitHub-specific.
rows.required: Add provider-neutral hosting capabilities if in scope, with real read/review/create workflows for each supported host.

rows.t3: T3 exposes provisioning and branch/environment controls.
rows.mako: Mako deliberately excludes a worktree manager under AGENTS.md. Internal isolated task workspaces are supported.
rows.required: An all-features claim conflicts with the current product contract; do not silently add a worktree manager.

rows.t3: T3 has environment authentication, pairing and remote UI flows.
rows.mako: Mako has a provider-neutral relay, tenant/device tokens and Slack/backend adapters; same-product remote UI behavior is not established.
rows.required: Compare pairing, reconnect, lease loss, attachment transfer, cancellation and native/remote consistency.

rows.t3: The inspected V2 branch has a scheduled-task service; main parity is not inferred from that branch.
rows.mako: Mako has persisted automations and settings UI; scheduler semantics are not matched.
rows.required: Test sleep/wake, missed runs, duplicate execution, active-session overlap and delivery under restart.

rows.t3: T3 has PTY manager/adapters and persistent UI contexts.
rows.mako: Mako has a bounded terminal daemon and restart tests. The reported memory spike has not been attributed; current daemon footprint was small.
rows.required: Run bounded output, backpressure, client disconnect and long-session soak with process-tree physical footprint accounting.

rows.t3: T3 has session-scoped MCP integration and provider configuration.
rows.mako: Mako has a redacted neutral MCP registry, provider-owned skill roots and trusted local UI extensions.
rows.required: Compare OAuth expiry, MCP replacement during sessions, secret redaction, tool errors and skill discovery across providers.

rows.t3: T3 has first-run/welcome flows and provider-instance setup.
rows.mako: Mako has provider/browser settings, but equivalent end-to-end first-run installation and recovery were not verified.
rows.required: Fresh-user setup: missing CLI, expired login, denied permission, no repository and first successful task, without developer intervention.

rows.t3: T3 uses accessible controls and dedicated UI tests; this is not an audited conformance claim.
rows.mako: Mako uses Radix dialogs and a command registry. Latest task dialog has no completed keyboard/screen-reader run.
rows.required: Audit focus order/restoration, nested overlays, announcements, zoom, reduced motion and keyboard-only operation.

rows.t3: T3 has updater and platform-specific desktop implementations.
rows.mako: Mako build configuration exists; this pass neither installed a release nor verified packaged SDK/permissions. Windows/Linux behavior is not established.
rows.required: Build and test an isolated package on each advertised platform, including SDK executable paths, signing/update and native permissions.

rows.t3: T3 has coalescing and stable UI techniques. No equal-workload benchmark was executed.
rows.mako: Mako has bounded readers, coalescing and performance tests. The application-memory incident invalidates any broad stability claim.
rows.required: Matched cold start, 10k threads, long transcript streaming, large repository and multi-hour soak; report RSS plus physical footprint/swap and p50/p95.

rows.t3: T3 has authorization and pairing policies. These have not been comparatively penetration-tested.
rows.mako: Mako tests host input, tenant/lease ownership and target isolation. Passing selected tests is not a broad security audit.
rows.required: Threat-model native/remote/extension boundaries and test unauthorized target use, secret leakage, replay and hostile tool output.

rows.t3: No matched T3 task suite was run in this pass.
rows.mako: Mako has individual successful real-provider fixtures, not a comparative quality or cost result.
rows.required: Same model/version, effort, prompts, repository, tools and budget; measure completion, regressions, retries, tokens, latency and user interventions.
